 MT Newswires Mon, 16 November 2026 at 10:24 pm GMT-6 1 min read MT Newswires -Shutterstock Singapore's merchandise trade surplus ballooned to SG$19.3 billion in October from SG$9.03 billion in September, according to data from Enterprise Singapore released on Tuesday. 
The latest figure exceeded Trading Economics' forecast of a SG$7.90 billion surplus.
Non-oil domestic exports (NODX) surged 79.8% year over year in October, extending the 68.3% increase in September. 
The expansion was driven by non-electronic exports, particularly structures of ships and boats and pharmaceuticals, while electronics continued to grow on sustained demand related to artificial intelligence.
Electronic NODX increased 73.9% year over year, following a 107.6% expansion in September. 
Non-electronic NODX rose 81.9%, accelerating from 54.1% in the previous month. For the first ten months of 2026, NODX grew 33.6% from a year earlier.
Among electronic products, disk media products, personal computers and integrated circuits recorded increases of 189.6%, 81.0% and 53.1%, respectively. 
Within non-electronic exports, pharmaceuticals rose 253.1%, while specialized machinery increased 57.3%. The growth in the number of ships and boats was also a key contributor.
Meanwhile, non-oil re-exports (NORX) increased 48.1% year-over-year in October, following a 47.8% rise in September. 
The expansion was driven mainly by electronics, which grew 69.1%, while non-electronic re-exports increased 15.0%.
Total merchandise trade rose 50.7% year over year in October, following a 50.8% expansion in September. Total exports increased 55.8%, while imports grew 44.9%.
NODX to the US, China and Taiwan expanded during the month, while shipments to India, Indonesia and Thailand contracted.
